title: Void Ending in a Square to Pluto
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The square is one of the two worst aspects in the lunar doctrine, an enmity the text grades as moderate because the signs it joins stand two natures apart. The counsel that guards every election runs exactly here: watch the square and the opposition in everything, and keep the Moon from the unfortunate planets in these figures above all.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a square to Pluto, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his buried endings. Pluto is unknown to Picatrix, found in 1930 and outside the world the book describes at every point. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of Picatrix's doctrine, never the source's own words. Named for the Roman lord of the underworld, it is read as the far, dark hinge of the set: a course that closes on it ends in the buried kind of ending, the small death of a matter before the next sign begins.
